full_text_en:
Li Jianguo v. Meng Fansheng, Changchun Shengxiang Construction Engineering Co., Ltd., et al. — Action for Objection to Enforcement by a Third Party

Ruling Summary

1. Legal rules are value judgment standards established by the legislative body after comprehensive consideration and trade-offs, and shall become rules with universal application in judicial practice. Unless otherwise specifically provided by law, they shall not be affected by certain special circumstances or established facts when applied.

2. The property of a branch company is the property of the company, and the civil liability of a branch company shall be borne by the company. This is the basic rule established by the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. A branch registered in accordance with law under its own name shall be governed by this rule. The internal agreements between a branch and the company concerning the division of rights, obligations, and liabilities cannot, because they are insufficient to challenge the public notice effect of the branch's registration in accordance with law, further cannot challenge third parties.

3. Those who abide by and act in accordance with the law shall have their legitimate rights and interests protected by law; those who do not abide by the law or even violate the law, because they disregard or even ignore legal rules, shall bear the risk of not being protected by law or being subject to legal sanction.

4. The contracting or leasing operations protected under Article 78 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution of Work by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) shall be those forms of contracting or leasing permitted by law. Where an enterprise or individual borrows the qualification of a construction enterprise under the guise of contracting or leasing, because this violates the relevant laws and judicial interpretations, it shall not be included within the scope of protection of that article.

5. An actual constructor is a concept stipulated in the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts. Because of the specific nature of the circumstances regulated, it is only appropriate to determine the status of an actual constructor in a dispute over a construction project construction contract governed by that Interpretation.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2016) Supreme People's Court Civil Retrial No. 149

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Meng Fansheng, male, Han ethnicity, born June 17, 1970, residing in Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Meng Jun, lawyer of Jilin Chuangyi Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Yu Honghua, lawyer of Jilin Chuangyi Law Firm.

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Changchun Shengxiang Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (formerly Changchun Dongya Construction Engineering Co., Ltd.). Domicile: 7 km on Changbai Highway, Luyuan District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Zhang Shiqi, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Agent ad litem: Qiao Hongbo, male, staff of the company.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Li Jianguo, male, Han ethnicity, born June 30, 1961, residing in Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Chen Wenlei, lawyer of Jilin Yingchun Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Changchun Teng'an Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. Domicile: Fifth Floor, Section 167, No. 57, Changjiang Road, Changjiang Road Economic Development Zone, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Guorong, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Retrial applicants Meng Fansheng and Changchun Shengxiang Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Shengxiang Company), in the case of an action for objection to enforcement by a third party against respondent Li Jianguo and defendant at first instance Changchun Teng'an Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Teng'an Company), disagreed with the civil judgment (2015) Ji Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 72 of the Higher People's Court of Jilin Province (hereinafter referred to as Jilin High Court) and applied to this Court for retrial. This Court, by civil ruling (2015) Min Shen Zi No. 2547 dated December 17, 2015, decided to bring the case up for retrial, and, in accordance with law, formed a collegiate bench with presiding judge Su Ge, and presiding judges Li Mingyi and Zhang Nengbao, with court assistant Song Ruqing assisting throughout the case handling, and clerk Ji Weiwei recording the case, and held a public hearing on July 14, 2016. Retrial applicant Meng Fansheng and his agents ad litem Meng Jun and Yu Honghua, retrial applicant Shengxiang Company's agent ad litem Qiao Hongbo, respondent Li Jianguo and his agent ad litem Chen Wenlei appeared in court for trial. Defendant at first instance Teng'an Company, after being served with the summons by public announcement of this Court, did not appear in court without justifiable reasons. This case is now concluded.

Li Jianguo filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Changchun City, Jilin Province (hereinafter referred to as Changchun Intermediate Court), alleging: In the case of a dispute over a sales contract between Meng Fansheng and Changchun Dongya Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (the predecessor of Shengxiang Company, hereinafter referred to as Dongya Company) and Teng'an Company, the Changchun Intermediate Court, by civil ruling (2012) Chang Min Si Chu Zi No. 2-6, froze the bank account deposit of Dongya Company's Jianhe Branch (hereinafter referred to as Jianhe Branch) in the amount of RMB 5,050,435.10. However, the relationship between Jianhe Branch and Dongya Company was a contracting relationship. Li Jianguo, as the actual investor of Jianhe Branch, owned the ownership of the frozen property, and therefore filed an objection to enforcement in accordance with law. The Changchun Intermediate Court made an enforcement ruling (2014) Chang Zhi Yi Zi No. 16, rejecting Li Jianguo's objection application. For this reason, according to Article 78 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Execution of Work by the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation) (hereinafter referred to as the "Execution Provisions"), Li Jianguo filed this lawsuit, requesting that in the enforcement case (2013) Chang Zhi Zi No. 155 of the Changchun Intermediate Court, the enforcement of the deposit of RMB 5,050,435.10 in the bank account of Jianhe Branch be stopped, and the freeze on that sum be lifted.

Meng Fansheng replied: Li Jianguo was not the contractor of Jianhe Branch, and requested that his claim be rejected and the enforcement of the deposit in Jianhe Branch's account continue.

Dongya Company replied: Jianhe Branch was a branch of Dongya Company. The property of a branch is part of the property of the parent company. Li Jianguo was merely the responsible person of Jianhe Branch. Although Dongya Company and Jianhe Branch had signed an internal contracting contract, the relationship between the two was not the contracting relationship stipulated in Article 78 of the Execution Provisions.

Teng'an Company submitted a written reply: Teng'an Company was not a proper defendant in this case. The freezing and enforcement of Dongya Company's accounts resulted from Meng Fansheng's application. Whether the freeze should be lifted and enforcement stopped had no relation to Teng'an Company. Teng'an Company did not oppose anyone's claim of rights over this property. The defendant should be Dongya Company, and Teng'an Company should not be named as a defendant.

The Changchun Intermediate Court found at first instance: On January 9, 2012, Meng Fansheng and Gan Yu filed a lawsuit with the Changchun Intermediate Court against Dongya Company, Teng'an Company, and Dongya Company's Xiangze Branch (hereinafter referred to as Xiangze Branch) over a sales contract dispute. On September 28, 2012, the Changchun Intermediate Court rendered a civil judgment (2012) Chang Min Si Chu Zi No. 2: "1. Dongya Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, pay Meng Fansheng steel material payment of RMB 7,319,306.20 and liquidated damages (calculated at 30% above the same-period benchmark interest rate for loans of the People's Bank of China from September 2, 2010 to the date of effectiveness of this judgment); 2. Teng'an Company shall bear joint and several guaranty liability for the payment of the above sums by Dongya Company, and after Teng'an Company performs the guaranty liability, it has the right to seek recourse from the debtor; 3. Meng Fansheng's other claims are rejected. If the monetary payment obligation is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, the debt interest for the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 229 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the 'Civil Procedure Law'). The case acceptance fee of RMB 110,715 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000, totaling RMB 115,715, shall be borne by Dongya Company." On December 18, 2012, the Changchun Intermediate Court made a civil ruling (2012) Chang Min Si Chu Zi No. 2-6, freezing the deposit in Jianhe Branch's account 0710XXXXXXXXXXXXX0396 at Jiutai Rural Commercial Bank, Changchun Avenue Sub-branch, in the amount of RMB 8.5 million, with an actual freeze of RMB 5,850,435.10. The said RMB 8.5 million was the project payment for the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project transferred to Jianhe Branch by the Housing Development Center of the Air Force Officers of the Shenyang Military Region on December 17, 2012. Because Li Guobin and Li Jianguo provided two houses owned by them as replacement guarantees, the Changchun Intermediate Court made a civil ruling (2012) Chang Min Si Chu Zi No. 2-8, lifting the freeze on RMB 800,000 of the RMB 5,850,435.10 deposit in Jianhe Branch's account. On June 5, 2013, Meng Fansheng applied to the Changchun Intermediate Court for enforcement, case number (2013) Chang Zhi Zi No. 155. During the enforcement process, Li Jianguo filed an objection, arguing that the frozen sum of RMB 5,850,435.10 was the income derived from Li Jianguo's contracting of Jianhe Branch and the construction of the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project, and requested the court to lift the freeze on that sum. On May 14, 2014, the Changchun Intermediate Court made an enforcement ruling (2014) Chang Zhi Yi Zi No. 16, rejecting Li Jianguo's objection.

Further found: Dongya Company was established on July 9, 1993, as a limited liability company, with a business scope of undertaking domestic and foreign construction projects. On March 17, 2006, Dongya Company applied to the Changchun Administration for Industry and Commerce to establish a branch, Jianhe Branch. On March 24, 2006, the Changchun Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a business license for Jianhe Branch, with a business scope of undertaking engineering contracting operations within the business scope of the company to which it belongs, and its civil liability shall be borne by the company to which it belongs. The responsible person of Jianhe Branch was initially Tian Wanhe, then changed to Li Jianguo on May 29, 2013. On March 4, 2011, Dongya Company signed a "Shenyang Military Region Air Force Construction and Installation Engineering Contract" with the Changchun Office of the Housing Development Center of the Air Force Officers of the Shenyang Military Region, undertaking the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project, with a contract price of RMB 83,561,772.

Further found: After its establishment, Jianhe Branch signed an "Internal Contracting Contract of Changchun Dongya Construction Engineering Co., Ltd." with Dongya Company, stipulating that the scope of the contract was industrial and civil building construction within the scope prescribed in the "Qualification Certificate"; Jianhe Branch was to pay Dongya Company an annual business fee of RMB 30,000 and an annual project fee of RMB 100,000.

The Changchun Intermediate Court held at first instance: (1) On the issue of the relationship between Dongya Company and Jianhe Branch. Li Jianguo claimed that the two had a contracting relationship; Dongya Company and Meng Fansheng claimed that the two were a parent company and its branch under unified operation and management. From the statements of the parties in this case, in the hearing of the preliminary case (2014) Chang Zhi Yi Zi No. 16, Dongya Company clearly admitted that for the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project, "the project was carried out by Li Jianguo," and had no objections to Li Jianguo's various claims and the evidence provided. Pursuant to Article 74 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Evidence Provisions"): "During the litigation process, the facts unfavorable to the party and the evidence recognized in the complaint, defense, statements and the submissions of the agent ad litem shall be confirmed by the court, unless the party withdraws and provides sufficient contrary evidence to overturn them." In the trial of this case, Dongya Company did not provide sufficient evidence to overturn all its claims made in the case (2014) Chang Zhi Yi Zi No. 16, so the statements in that case should prevail. From the evidence in this case, Jianhe Branch in the industrial and commercial registration is a branch lawfully registered and established by Dongya Company. According to the relevant provisions of the Company Law, a branch is an institution established by a company in a place other than its domicile to carry out activities in its own name, subject to the jurisdiction of the parent company in terms of business, funds, personnel, etc., without independent legal personality, without legal or economic independence, without its own name or articles of association, without its own property, and its debts are borne by the parent company's assets. Li Jianguo provided evidence that Jianhe Branch paid management fees to Dongya Company annually, which Dongya Company also acknowledged. The fact that Jianhe Branch paid management fees to the parent company contradicted its status as a branch of Dongya Company. Dongya Company stated that the relationship between it and Jianhe Branch was an internal contracting relationship and they signed an internal contracting contract. However, the parties to the internal contracting contract were Dongya Company as Party A and Jianhe Branch as Party B, and the subject of the contract was "industrial and civil building construction within the scope prescribed in the 'Qualification Certificate'," which was not aimed at completing specific work and did not meet the basic characteristics of a contracting contract. Therefore, it could not be determined that the relationship between Dongya Company and Jianhe Branch was an internal contracting relationship. Dongya Company could not clearly state basic company information such as Jianhe Branch's office premises, office environment, personnel management, specific business development, etc., nor could it provide evidence of direct management by Dongya Company over Jianhe Branch's personnel and property, nor could it provide relevant accounts of Jianhe Branch, nor could it provide evidence of Dongya Company's specific input, construction, and management of the projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch. Therefore, combined with the fact that Dongya Company collected management fees from Jianhe Branch, it could be determined that the relationship between Dongya Company and Jianhe Branch was not an ordinary parent company-branch relationship, but that Dongya Company had contracted out Jianhe Branch, did not conduct unified operation and management of Jianhe Branch, and achieved profits from Jianhe Branch through the collection of management fees.

(2) On the issue of the contractor of Jianhe Branch. Tian Wanhe, the former responsible person of Jianhe Branch, confirmed in the inquiry record of the Changchun Intermediate Court that since the establishment of Jianhe Branch, Li Jianguo was the actual investor, all projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch were negotiated by Li Jianguo personally, and were also funded and organized by him, with Dongya Company only collecting management fees. The certification materials provided by Li Jianguo from the Xin Yuan Branch of Jilin Yanfang Real Estate Group Co., Ltd. and from the Changchun Office of Shenyang Military Region all confirmed that the Jindalai Xiaoqu, Wenyuan Xiaoqu, and Lantian Jia Yuan Phases I and II projects were negotiated, organized, and constructed by Li Jianguo personally, and partial funds were advanced by him. The bank deposit account information and detailed account inquiry records of China Construction Bank, as well as receipts for expenses related to the Lantian Jia Yuan Xiaoqu project, also corroborated the above facts. At the same time, Li Jianguo applied for witnesses Yang Dianfu, Meng Dejun, and Zeng Zhongyuan to testify in court, confirming that they had subcontracted the civil engineering, woodwork, and plastering work of the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project from Li Jianguo, and the arrears of migrant workers' wages were always claimed from Li Jianguo personally. The three witnesses were not familiar with Dongya Company or Jianhe Branch. Li Jianguo also provided relevant evidence of cash expenditures for part of the project funds advanced by him personally. In addition, Dongya Company, Meng Fansheng, and Teng'an Company all did not provide evidence to prove that any person other than Li Jianguo claimed rights over the contracting of Jianhe Branch. Therefore, although Li Jianguo did not provide a contract signed between him and Dongya Company for contracting Jianhe Branch, combined with the evidence he provided on investment, management, organization, and construction of the projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch, and the testimonies of Tian Wanhe, Yang Dianfu, Meng Dejun, and Zeng Zhongyuan, it could be determined that Li Jianguo was the actual contractor of Jianhe Branch.

(3) Li Jianguo, as the actual contractor of Jianhe Branch, had rights over the property under the name of Jianhe Branch. The RMB 5,050,435.10 in dispute in this case was the project payment for the Lantian Jia Yuan Phase II project transferred by the Changchun Office of the Shenyang Military Region to Jianhe Branch's account, and was Li Jianguo's input and income in the process of contracting Jianhe Branch. Article 78 of the Execution Provisions provides: "When a branch of an enterprise legal person, as the person subject to enforcement, cannot pay its debts, the enterprise legal person may be ruled as the person subject to enforcement. If the property directly managed by the enterprise legal person itself is still insufficient to pay its debts, the people's court may rule to enforce the property of other branches of the enterprise legal person. If it is necessary to enforce the property of a branch of an enterprise legal person that has been contracted or leased, the input and due income of the contractor or lessee shall be protected in accordance with law." Therefore, Li Jianguo had civil rights and interests in the subject matter of enforcement sufficient to exclude enforcement, and the enforcement of the deposit of RMB 5,050,435.10 in Jianhe Branch's account at Jiutai Rural Commercial Bank, Changchun Avenue Sub-branch, account number 0710XXXXXXXXXXXXXX3906, frozen in the enforcement case (2013) Chang Zhi Zi No. 155, should be stopped. Li Jianguo's request to lift the freeze on the said sum did not fall within the scope of trial in this action for objection to enforcement.

In summary, the Changchun Intermediate Court, in accordance with Article 78 of the Execution Provisions, Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law, Article 312 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the "Civil Procedure Law Interpretation"), Article 19 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law in the Enforcement Procedure, and Article 74 of the Civil Evidence Provisions, ruled: In the enforcement case (2013) Chang Zhi Zi No. 155, the deposit of RMB 5,050,435.10 in the account of Dongya Company's Jianhe Branch at Jiutai Rural Commercial Bank, Changchun Avenue Sub-branch, account number 0710XXXXXXXXXXXXXX3906, shall not be enforced. Case acceptance fee RMB 47,153, to be borne by Meng Fansheng in the amount of RMB 23,576.50, and by Dongya Company in the amount of RMB 23,576.50.

Meng Fansheng did not accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to Jilin High Court, requesting: to set aside the original judgment, reject Li Jianguo's claims, and order Li Jianguo to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Reasons: Li Jianguo's evidence was insufficient to support his claims. The first-instance court erred in placing the burden of proof on the parent company Shengxiang Company, incorrectly allocating the burden of proof; the findings of fact were clearly erroneous and without basis. The first-instance court incorrectly understood and applied the law, violating the basic principles of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the legislative intent of the Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretations.

Shengxiang Company also did not accept the first-instance judgment and appealed to Jilin High Court, requesting: to set aside the original judgment, reject Li Jianguo's claims, and order Li Jianguo to bear the litigation costs of the first and second instances. Reasons: The first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact. The contracting contract signed between Jianhe Branch and Shengxiang Company was only a form of internal management of the company and did not change the relationship between the parent company and its branch. Moreover, Li Jianguo was not the actual contractor. The property involved in the case was an asset of Shengxiang Company, not Li Jianguo's "input and income." The first-instance judgment applied the law incorrectly.

Li Jianguo replied: The first-instance judgment found clear facts, applied the law correctly, and followed proper procedures. He requested that the judgment be upheld.

The Jilin High Court confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court at the second instance.

The Jilin High People's Court held at second instance that: Jianhe Branch is a lawfully registered branch of Shengxiang Company, and the relationship between them is naturally that of a parent company and its branch. The key issue in this case is whether Jianhe Branch was contracted out to another person and whether the RMB 5,050,435.10 deposit in the branch's account constituted that contractor's investment and income. The distinctive feature of a contracting-out arrangement is that the contractor manages the business and bears the operational risks and rewards, whereas a branch that is not contracted out should be managed by the parent company, which bears the operational risks and rewards. In this case, although the parties to the "Internal Contracting Agreement" were Shengxiang Company and Jianhe Branch, the subject matter of the contract was Jianhe Branch itself; thus, it is illogical for Jianhe Branch to be a party to this contract as the signing entity. Based on the facts that Shengxiang Company collected management fees and taxes from Jianhe Branch, that Shengxiang Company admitted during trial that all profits generated by Jianhe Branch, after deducting various expenses, were distributed to Jianhe Branch, and that Shengxiang Company could not clearly explain in court how Jianhe Branch was established or managed, it can be determined that Shengxiang Company had contracted Jianhe Branch to its de facto controller.

Tian Wanhe, the former responsible person of Jianhe Branch, testified at first instance that since its establishment, Li Jianguo had been the actual investor, that all projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch were negotiated personally by Li Jianguo, and that Li Jianguo also provided the upfront funds and organized the workers for construction. The Xinyuan Branch of Jilin Province Yanfang Real Estate Group Co., Ltd. and the Changchun Office of the Shenyang Military Region provided evidence confirming that the Jindacai Community, Wenyuan Community, and the first and second phases of Lantian Jiayuan Community were negotiated, organized, and constructed by Li Jianguo personally, and that he also advanced part of the payments. At first instance, three witnesses, Yang Dianfu, Meng Dejun, and Zeng Zhongyuan, testified in court, confirming that they had obtained contracts for civil construction, carpentry, and plastering work for the second phase of Lantian Jiayuan Community from Li Jianguo, and that the overdue wages for migrant workers had always been claimed from Li Jianguo personally. Additionally, Li Jianguo submitted a China Construction Bank deposit account information and detailed statement inquiry sheet, receipts for expenses related to the Lantian Jiayuan Community project, and relevant evidence of cash payments advanced by Li Jianguo for part of the project funds, all of which could prove that Li Jianguo, as the de facto controller of Jianhe Branch, carried out the construction work on the disputed project. In contrast, although Meng Fansheng and Shengxiang Company claimed that Shengxiang Company was the actual constructor of the disputed project, they were unable to provide any relevant evidence of specific investment, construction, or management for the projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch. They knew very little about the relevant circumstances of the project, and during the pre-litigation hearing in Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16, Shengxiang Company explicitly acknowledged that the disputed project in this case was constructed by Li Jianguo. Although Shengxiang Company produced a letter of undertaking from Li Jianguo to prove that its statement in the hearing of Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16 was not objective, the content of that letter of undertaking failed to address the issue of the actual constructor of the disputed project. The letter of undertaking could not support Shengxiang Company's change of position. Pursuant to Article 74 of the Provisions on Civil Evidence, which states: "During litigation, facts unfavorable to a party and evidence acknowledged by that party in the complaint, answer, statements, and the pleadings of its agent ad litem shall be confirmed by the people's court, unless the party retracts and provides sufficient contrary evidence to overturn them," the court of first instance correctly allocated the burden of proof to Shengxiang Company. Given that Li Jianguo provided substantial evidence to prove that he was the actual constructor of the disputed project, that Meng Fansheng failed to provide any evidence regarding the actual constructor of the disputed project, and that Shengxiang Company did not provide sufficient evidence to overturn its statement in Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16, the court of first instance did not err in finding that Li Jianguo was the actual constructor of the disputed project. In conclusion, it can be determined that the RMB 5,050,435.10 in project funds for the second phase of Lantian Jiayuan Community, which was transferred by the Changchun Office of the Shenyang Military Region into account number 0710XXXXXXXXXXXXXX3906 of Jianhe Branch, constituted Li Jianguo's investment and income during his contracting of Jianhe Branch. Pursuant to Article 78 of the Provisions on Enforcement, which states: "If the branch of an enterprise legal person that is the judgment debtor cannot satisfy the debt, the people's court may rule that the enterprise legal person is the judgment debtor. If the property directly managed by the enterprise legal person is still insufficient to satisfy the debt, the people's court may rule to execute the property of other branches of the enterprise legal person. If it is necessary to execute the property of a branch of an enterprise legal person that has been contracted or leased out, the investment and due income of the contractor or lessee shall be protected in accordance with law," the court of first instance did not err in ruling that, in the enforcement case (2013) Changzhizhi No. 155, the deposit of RMB 5,050,435.10 in account number 0710XXXXXXXXXXXXXX3906 of Jianhe Branch at Jiutai Rural Commercial Bank, Changchun Avenue Sub-branch, should not be subject to enforcement.

In summary, the Jilin High People's Court held that the judgment of first instance had clear findings of fact, correct application of law, and lawful trial procedures. Pursuant to Article 170, paragraph 1, item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, the court ruled: appeal dismissed; judgment of first instance affirmed. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 94,306 was to be borne by Meng Fansheng (RMB 47,153) and by Shengxiang Company (RMB 47,153).

Meng Fansheng applied to this Court for retrial on the following grounds: Pursuant to Article 200, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law, he applied for retrial, requesting that the original judgment be reversed and that Li Jianguo's claims be dismissed in accordance with law, and that all litigation costs in this case be borne by Li Jianguo.

His main arguments were:

(1) The original judgment found that Li Jianguo was an independent contractor of Jianhe Branch without sufficient evidence. Shengxiang Company never acknowledged that Li Jianguo was the contractor or investor of Jianhe Branch, and Li Jianguo also failed to prove that he had personally entered into a contracting or leasing agreement with Shengxiang Company or Jianhe Branch. The original judgment clearly erred in relying on Shengxiang Company's statement in the hearing of Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16 as important evidence. The labor contracts, filing procedures, and financial statements for a series of engineering and financial personnel submitted by Shengxiang Company in the course of operating and managing Jianhe Branch, combined with Li Jianguo's letter of undertaking, were sufficient to prove that Jianhe Branch was not independently contracted by Li Jianguo and to overturn Shengxiang Company's prior statement in the enforcement hearing.

(2) The original judgment misunderstood and misapplied Article 78 of the Provisions on Enforcement, constituting an error in the application of law. According to that provision, even if a branch of a judgment debtor is lawfully contracted or leased out, it does not mean that execution is absolutely prohibited; rather, it is necessary to ascertain and protect the contractor's lawful investment rights and interests. The evidence provided by Shengxiang Company could prove that the Shenyang Military Region Lantian Jiayuan Community project still had over RMB 7 million in unpaid taxes, and multiple effective judgments had ordered Shengxiang Company to assume the debts and liabilities of Jianhe Branch. The project funds recovered by Jianhe Branch were insufficient to cover costs and repay debts, let alone constitute investment income.

Shengxiang Company applied to this Court for retrial on the following grounds: Pursuant to Article 200, items (2) and (6) of the Civil Procedure Law, it applied for retrial, requesting that the original judgment be reversed and that Li Jianguo's claims be dismissed in accordance with law, and that all litigation costs in this case be borne by Li Jianguo.

Its main arguments were:

(1) The original judgment found that the disputed funds were Li Jianguo's personal income without sufficient evidence. The disputed funds were project funds allocated by the construction unit to Shengxiang Company, and it was an undisputed fact that the unpaid tax on invoices for the Shenyang Military Region Lantian Jiayuan project was RMB 7,867,894. The original judgment erroneously treated the disputed funds as personal income.

(2) The original judgment made an error in the application of law. The internal contracting agreement was an internal management requirement and mechanism of Shengxiang Company; only Shengxiang Company, as the parent company, could bear civil liability externally. In lawsuits or arbitrations arising from Jianhe Branch, Shengxiang Company was consistently ordered or adjudicated to assume the liabilities that Jianhe Branch should have borne.

Li Jianguo responded jointly to the retrial applications of Meng Fansheng and Shengxiang Company, arguing that the retrial applications of the two applicants lacked factual and legal support and should be dismissed.

His main arguments were:

(1) The original judgment's assessment of the evidence from the enforcement objection hearing in Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16 was not improper. During the review of that enforcement objection, Shengxiang Company submitted evidentiary materials proving that during 2010-2013, Li Jianguo independently contracted Jianhe Branch and had independent rights to income. However, in the first-instance trial of this case, Shengxiang Company submitted a letter of undertaking dated March 27, 2014, from Li Jianguo, stating that 'the certification issued by Dongya Company is only for use in litigation,' in an attempt to prove that its statement in the enforcement objection hearing of Case No. (2014) Changzhiyizi No. 16 was not objective, but the evidence was insufficient. The labor contracts and personnel filing procedures for engineering and financial personnel submitted by Shengxiang Company were not related to Jianhe Branch because those personnel were not employees of Jianhe Branch. The financial statements and other evidence were self-generated by Shengxiang Company and lacked objectivity; they could not overturn the fact that Jianhe Branch had been actually contracted by Li Jianguo and that the disputed deposit was Li Jianguo's income as the actual constructor. The court of first instance correctly applied Article 74 of the Provisions on Civil Evidence.

(2) The burden of proof allocation by the courts of first and second instance was correct and did not violate legal provisions. This case is an enforcement objection lawsuit. Li Jianguo raised an objection to the ownership of the deposits in the sealed bank account of Jianhe Branch, claiming that the deposit was not the property of Jianhe Branch but rather Li Jianguo's personal income as the actual contractor of Jianhe Branch. To prove his claim, Li Jianguo submitted a series of evidence to the court. Meng Fansheng and Shengxiang Company, as defendants at first instance, should also submit evidence to prove their own claims. Pursuant to Article 64, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law, and Articles 2, paragraphs 3 and 4, and Article 7 of the Provisions on Civil Evidence, the courts of first and second instance correctly allocated the burden of proof.

(3) The original judgment's finding that Li Jianguo was the actual contractor of Jianhe Branch and that the disputed funds were Li Jianguo's income as the actual constructor was factually clear and legally correct. The subject matter of the 'Internal Contracting Agreement' between Shengxiang Company and Jianhe Branch was Jianhe Branch itself; therefore, it was illogical for Jianhe Branch to be a party to the contract. Under the terms of the agreement, Shengxiang Company collected management fees and taxes from Jianhe Branch, and Shengxiang Company also admitted that all profits generated by Jianhe Branch, after deducting various expenses, were left to Jianhe Branch. Thus, the substantive nature of the contracting agreement was that Li Jianguo, as the contractor of Jianhe Branch, entered into the agreement with Shengxiang Company regarding the contracting relationship.

The disputed deposit in Jianhe Branch's bank account was the project funds for the Lantian Jiayuan Community allocated by the Changchun Office of the Shenyang Military Region, which also issued a certificate confirming that the project was negotiated, organized, constructed, and funded by Li Jianguo personally. Combined with the substantial other evidence submitted by Li Jianguo, all of this could prove that the funds should be Li Jianguo's personal income. In contrast, Shengxiang Company was unable to provide any relevant evidence of specific investment, construction, or management for the projects undertaken by Jianhe Branch.

Changchun Teng'an Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. did not submit a written statement before the hearing.

Upon retrial, this Court confirms the facts found by the Changchun Intermediate People's Court in the original first instance.

This Court is of the opinion that, based on the retrial requests of Meng Fansheng and Shengxiang Company, and in light of Li Jianguo's response, the issue in dispute in this case is whether Li Jianguo's enforcement objection to the disputed funds in Jianhe Branch's account is established and sufficient to prevent the people's court from enforcing execution.

This Court holds:

(1) Jianhe Branch is a branch of Shengxiang Company, and the relationship between them is subject to the adjustment of the Company Law. Article 14, paragraph 1 of the Company Law provides: 'A company may establish branches. When establishing a branch, the company shall apply to the company registration authority for registration and obtain a business license. A branch does not have legal personality, and its civil liability shall be borne by the company.' Pursuant to the above provisions, the property of a branch belongs to the company, and the civil liability arising from the branch's external civil activities is borne by the company. Article 78, paragraph 1 of the Provisions on Enforcement also provides that if a branch of an enterprise legal person that is the judgment debtor cannot satisfy the debt, the people's court may rule that the enterprise legal person is the judgment debtor. Similarly, if the judgment debtor is an enterprise legal person, failing to execute the property of its branch would violate the principle of reciprocity of rights and obligations.

Based on the facts found, Shengxiang Company (formerly Dongya Company) applied to the Changchun Administration for Industry and Commerce on March 17, 2006, to establish a branch, Jianhe Branch. On March 24, 2006, the Changchun Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a business license for Jianhe Branch, with the business scope of engaging in engineering contracting within the business scope of the affiliated company, and its civil liability is to be borne by the affiliated company. Since Jianhe Branch was lawfully registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce as a branch of Shengxiang Company, a legal relationship between the company and branch, as established by the Company Law, existed between Shengxiang Company and Jianhe Branch. This relationship is subject to the rules governing companies and branches set forth in the Company Law. Specifically: the property of the branch is the property of the company, and the civil liability of the branch is borne by the company. This Court also notes that the underlying case in the enforcement application by retrial applicant Meng Fansheng was a dispute over a sales contract between him and Xiangze Branch. That judgment, based on Xiangze Branch being a branch of Shengxiang Company, ordered Shengxiang Company to assume the debt liability and subsequently executed Shengxiang Company's property. Li Jianguo stated at trial that the business model of several branches of Shengxiang Company was essentially the same, i.e., establishing branches in the form of registration to use Shengxiang Company's qualifications to undertake construction projects. In this context, if the rules of the Company Law regarding the relationship between a company and its branch are applied to one branch to impose liability on the company, but not applied to another branch to exempt it from liability, this would violate the principle of reciprocity of rights and obligations and the uniformity of the application of law.

(2) The internal agreement between Li Jianguo and Shengxiang Company regarding the operational model of Jianhe Branch has no legal effect against third parties. As previously stated, Jianhe Branch was lawfully registered with the administrative authority for industry and commerce as a branch of Shengxiang Company and is subject to the existing rules of the Company Law. Regardless of how the rights, obligations, and responsibility allocation between Shengxiang Company and Jianhe Branch were internally agreed upon, the content of such agreement is insufficient to override the public notice effect of its lawful registration with the administrative authority for industry and commerce and is therefore insufficient to oppose third parties. If Jianhe Branch or Li Jianguo believes that bearing responsibility for Shengxiang Company violates their internal agreement with Shengxiang Company, they may resolve the matter through consultation with Shengxiang Company.

Since Jianhe Branch is a branch of Shengxiang Company, and the disputed funds are within the bank account of Jianhe Branch, those funds are, as a matter of law, the property of Shengxiang Company. In the enforcement against Shengxiang Company, absent any statutory circumstance that would preclude enforcement, the people's court may execute those funds.

(3) The internal contracting agreement between Jianhe Branch and Shengxiang Company does not fall within the scope of a contracted-out branch of an enterprise legal person as referred to in Article 78 of the Provisions on Enforcement. First, the internal contracting agreement designates Jianhe Branch as the contractor and Shengxiang Company as the party being contracted out. In other words, based on the form of the agreement, the entity being contracted out is Shengxiang Company, and Jianhe Branch, as a branch of the enterprise legal person, is not contracted out. Moreover, based on the facts found, neither Shengxiang Company nor Jianhe Branch entered into any relevant contracting agreement with Li Jianguo. Therefore, the original judgment's finding that Li Jianguo was the actual contractor of Jianhe Branch lacks a contractual basis. Second, the scope of contracting under the internal contracting agreement is the industrial and civil construction scope specified in the 'Qualification Certificate.' In other words, the substantive nature of the agreement is that, while it is called an internal contracting agreement, it is in fact a lease or compensated use of the construction enterprise qualification. Li Jianguo also admitted at trial that his operation of Jianhe Branch primarily involved using Shengxiang Company's qualification to facilitate external contracting of construction projects. In other words, the substantive nature of the internal contracting agreement is not a legal contracting relationship. Third, the contracting or leasing operations referred to and protected by Article 78 of the Provisions on Enforcement should be those types of contracting or leasing that are permitted by law. As is well known, construction enterprises are highly specialized, and the quality of construction directly affects the safety of life and property of the people. Therefore, such enterprises are not only required to have registered capital in accordance with national provisions, but also to have the professional qualifications appropriate to the construction activities they engage in. In practice, the so-called contracting or leasing operations in some construction enterprises are, in substance, a cover for entities or individuals lacking qualifications to borrow the qualifications of a construction enterprise for construction. Because borrowing qualifications for construction is prohibited by law and judicial interpretations, the related contracting or leasing agreements and construction subcontracting agreements are also impermissible under law. Therefore, even if it could be determined that an actual contracting relationship existed between Li Jianguo and Jianhe Branch, because the form of such contracting operation is not permitted by law, it should not fall within the scope of contracting operations under Article 78 of the Provisions on Enforcement.

(4) Law, as a body of rules regulating human conduct, has an important value in protecting lawful rights and interests. This Court holds and advocates that those who abide by the law and act lawfully will have their lawful rights and interests protected by law; conversely, those who do not abide by or even violate the law, because they disregard or even ignore legal rules, should bear the risk of not being protected by law or even facing legal sanctions. Li Jianguo has full capacity for civil conduct and has been engaged in construction engineering for many years. He should know the laws and regulations of the state concerning construction engineering, the legal stance toward borrowing qualifications for construction, and the rights, obligations, and liability relationship between a company and its branch. However, he insisted on conducting business activities under the name of a branch of Shengxiang Company, insisted on using Shengxiang Company's qualification to undertake external construction projects, and insisted on engaging in such acts not permitted by law and obtaining income. He must bear the legal risk that such conduct may not be protected by law. Therefore, even if it could be determined that Li Jianguo was the de facto controller of Jianhe Branch, because he externally engaged in civil activities under the name of Jianhe Branch, and the disputed funds were actually deposited into Jianhe Branch's account, he must bear legal liability in accordance with existing legal rules. That is, his enforcement objection to the disputed funds is insufficient to prevent the people's court from enforcing execution.

In judicial practice, some cases often give rise to conflicts between established facts or special circumstances and existing legal rules. The reason why the courts of first and second instance in this case made the determinations in the original judgment was that they were influenced by the struggle of balancing interests triggered by such conflict. As analyzed in the original judgment, there indeed existed special circumstances between Shengxiang Company, Jianhe Branch, and Li Jianguo that differed from the general business model of a company and its branch. For example, as Li Jianguo himself stated, although he conducted business activities in the form of a branch, in reality, he personally borrowed the qualifications of Shengxiang Company to undertake construction of certain projects. From a certain perspective, his situation is also worthy of sympathy. However, this Court also holds that since legal rules are value standards established by the legislature after comprehensive weighing and selection, they should become rules with general applicability in judicial practice, should become tenets that judicial officers must always adhere to unless the law provides otherwise, and should become norms that are not affected by certain special circumstances or established facts. Otherwise, if a legal rule can constantly change and adapt to the special circumstances or established facts of individual cases, that rule will, due to its uncertainty, no longer be universally believed and willingly observed, thereby losing its significance of existence, and will seriously harm the authority of the law, the stability of order, and the fairness of justice.

(5) The original judgment's determination that Li Jianguo was the actual constructor of Phase II of the LanTianJiaYuan project exceeded the scope of trial in this case. The concept of "actual constructor" is a term stipulated in the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law for the Trial of Cases of Disputes over Construction Project Construction Contracts, which aims to provide limited protection to those who have actually constructed the disputed project but cannot claim project payments due to contractual relationships. Due to the specificity of the circumstances governed by this interpretation, it is appropriate to determine the status of an actual constructor only in cases of disputes over construction project construction contracts governed by such interpretation. This case is an action of execution objection by a third party, not a dispute over a construction project construction contract filed by an actual constructor against the developer and contractor as defendants. By determining Li Jianguo as the actual constructor of Phase II of the LanTianJiaYuan project, the original judgment, on the one hand, exceeded the scope of trial of this case; on the other hand, because the courts of first and second instance did not hear the case as a dispute over a construction project construction contract and did not conduct a trial, judgment, or ruling based on the claims and defenses of the parties involved in the project and the presentation and cross-examination of evidence, such determination may be unfair and may have a certain impact on the rights and obligations of the parties involved in the project. Therefore, the original judgment's determination that Li Jianguo was the actual constructor of Phase II of the LanTianJiaYuan project was inappropriate, and this Court hereby corrects it.

In summary, Jianhe Branch is a branch of Shengxiang Company, and the disputed funds in the account of Jianhe Branch are, in law, the property of Shengxiang Company. The internal contracting agreement between Jianhe Branch and Shengxiang Company does not have legal effect against third parties and should not be included within the scope of contracted operations under Article 78 of the Enforcement Provisions. The original judgment, by applying Article 78 of the Enforcement Provisions and determining that the disputed funds were Li Jianguo's personal property, committed an error in the application of law and should be corrected. Li Jianguo's objection to the disputed funds is insufficient to preclude the people's court from enforcing the execution. Pursuant to Article 14, Paragraph 1 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 207 and 227 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 312, Paragraph 1, Item 2, and Article 407, Paragraph 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2015) Ji Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 72 of the Jilin High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2014) Chang Min Er Chu Zi No. 5 of the Changchun Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province;

2. Reject Li Jianguo's claims.

The case acceptance fee of RMB 47,153 for first instance and RMB 94,306 for second instance shall be borne by Li Jianguo.

This judgment is final.
